subject: Technical recap & PoC scope — embeddings + function-calling prototype
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>
To: Emily Shore <emily.shore@veridian.ai>, procurement@veridian.ai
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Technical recap & PoC scope — embeddings + function-calling prototype

Hi Emily — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our call + proposed next steps so we have a shared reference. I captured the key pains, success metrics, and a minimal PoC scope we discussed.

Pain points you highlighted
- Search relevance: current semantic search returns too many false positives for clinical notes (precision ~58%).
- Cost/latency: maintenance budget for vector infra is tight; spikes in query volume cause unacceptable tails.
- Structured output needs: downstream systems require deterministic JSON that maps to specific fields (patient_id, note_summary, flags).

Goals/metrics for a successful PoC
- Relevance lift: 8–12% absolute precision improvement on your test set.
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms for single-item embedding rerank flows under typical load.
- Deterministic outputs: structured JSON with schema validation passing 95% of sampled responses.

Integration & product fit notes
- Embeddings/rerank: recommend Redwood embeddings + local reranker using the SDK endpoint (we can push an embeddings endpoint + a /rerank convenience wrapper that returns scores and ranks).
- Function calling: we’ll expose structured output via function-calling spec (OpenAPI-ish payload) so your pipeline can ingest parsed JSON directly. We identified two function signatures you care about — note_summary and clinical_flag_extraction.
- Streaming: for long-note summarization we’ll enable streaming tokens so UX teams can render progressive summaries while maintaining the final structured payload in the end.
- SDK changes: small additions requested — a rerank convenience client, and a function-schema validator hook. Alex flagged these as 1–2 sprint changes on our side.

Proposed PoC scope (4 weeks) — MVP
1) Ingest 5k de-identified notes from your test bucket into a temporary vector index (we’ll run this in Hosted with dedicated capacity).
2) Implement embeddings -> rerank pipeline using Redwood SDK (we’ll provide a sample integration spec).
3) Two function-call endpoints: note_summary and clinical_flag_extraction with strict JSON schema.
4) Basic dashboard: token and latency breakdown for the PoC dataset.

Dependencies we need from Veridian
- Sample dataset (deidentified) by EOD next Thu (2026-08-27)
- SOC2 questionnaire answered (we can share a subset for PoC)
- Point of contact for engineering deep-dive: Emily or an engineer you delegate

Next steps (I propose)
- I’ll schedule a 60-min technical deep dive with Alex + Monica (engineers) for Tue 8/25 or Wed 8/26. Please confirm availability.
- I attached a short integration spec + an OpenAPI function-calls snippet to demonstrate the payloads.
- We’ll stand up the trial index once we have the sample data and you sign the short PoC agreement.

Attachments: redwood-sample-integration-spec.pdf, openapi-function-calls-snippet.json

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0182

---
Redwood Inference — high-performance LLM inference for production
"Make inference predictable and economical."

From: Emily Shore <emily.shore@veridian.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@veridian.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Technical recap & PoC scope — embeddings + function-calling prototype

Thanks, Aditya — that summary is super helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications and asks from our side: 

Clarifications
- Precision target: the 8–12% lift is our ideal; minimum acceptable is +5% on the current test set.
- Data residency: PoC data must remain in us-west-2 and not be scanned by external indexing jobs. Is Redwood able to guarantee region pinning for the trial index?

Procurement/timeline
- We can provide the de-identified dataset by 8/27 as you requested, but procurement will need the short PoC agreement signed before we hand off S3 access. Procurement will also need an IP/data usage clause (we can send a redline).

Technical contact
- I’ll loop in our data engineer, Samir (samir.patel@veridian.ai), for the deep-dive if that’s OK — he’ll own the dataset handoff and verification.

A couple of quick asks for the PoC agreeement:
1) Confirm retention: PoC vectors must be deleted within 30 days of PoC completion unless we agree otherwise.
2) Provide an SLA statement for p95 inference latency (best-effort is fine for the trial, but we’d like an expected number).

If you can send the draft PoC agreement and confirm region pinning, we’ll fast-track the procurement side.

Best,
Emily Shore
Head of Data Products — Veridian Health
emily.shore@veridian.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>
To: Emily Shore <emily.shore@veridian.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@veridian.ai>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Technical recap & PoC scope — embeddings + function-calling prototype

Emily / Samir — great, thanks for the clarifications. Quick replies inline and an updated plan: 

Region pinning: yes — we can pin the PoC index to us-west-2 (Hosted Dedicated trial pool) and provide an export snapshot you control. I’ll note that in the PoC draft.

Retention: we’ll include a 30-day deletion clause in the PoC agreement and provide an automated deletion audit log.

SLA expectations (trial): p95 ~ 220–260ms for single-item embedding + rerank under the PoC dataset; we’ll include observed baseline numbers in the dashboard. For production we can discuss Dedicated SLA options in the contract.

Updated PoC timeline & commitments
- 8/25–8/26: technical deep-dive (60m) — Alex and Monica to run the session.
- 8/27: Veridian uploads dataset and procurement signs PoC agreement.
- Week of 8/31: Redwood stands up PoC index and delivers integration sample + starter code.
- Two weeks after index: joint evaluation using your metrics and dataset.

Action items (owners)
- Emily / Samir: confirm availability for 8/25–8/26 deep-dive and upload de-id sample to S3 by 8/27.
- Alex / Monica (Redwood): prepare sample SDK changes (rerank helper + function-schema validator) and a runbook for streaming summarization.
- Aditya: draft PoC agreement and send to procurement today (attached in next email).

I’ll send calendar invites for Tue/Wed options shortly (Alex, Monica — I put tentative slots on your calendars).

Thanks — quick, practical scope should let us measure the three metrics you care about.

Aditya

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.inference>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
Cc: Emily Shore <emily.shore@veridian.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@veridian.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Technical recap & PoC scope — embeddings + function-calling prototype

Quick internal notes (adding to thread so external folks see we’re aligned):
- SDK ETA: I can get the rerank helper and the function-schema validator into a preview branch by EOD 8/28. The helper will wrap embed->score->sort and return scores+rank indices.
- Streaming: we’ll use chunked responses for the progressive summary UI and emit a final function call payload at the end; will validate JSON schema before the final commit.
- Resource notes: recommend starting PoC on 1 dedicated GPU (A10g-ish) with continuous batching disabled to hit the p95 target; we’ll iterate if tail latency is higher.

I’ll post the preview branch and a short README to the Drive link after I push.

—Alex
